extracted.subtask_description: A wartime Associated Press news article reporting Allied battlefield activity and publishing the texts of Allied commands' orders on preservation of historic monuments, cultural sites, and rules for military use of listed buildings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for historic monuments (general principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Historic monuments and cultural heritage shall be respected insofar as operational conditions permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote: 'Today we are fighting in a country which has contributed a great deal to our cultural inheritance... We are bound to respect those monuments so far as war allows.' If choice is required between destroying a famous building and sacrificing our own men, men’s lives take precedence and the buildings must go; however, in many cases monuments can be spared without detriment to operational needs. The order emphasizes balancing operational necessity with preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict misuse of the phrase 'military necessity'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'military necessity' must not be used to cloak negligence, convenience, or personal convenience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote and admonition: 'The phrase “military necessity” is sometimes used where it would be more truthful to speak of military convenience or even of personal convenience. I do not want it to cloak slackness or indifference.' Commanders should avoid treating 'military necessity' as a blanket justification for avoidable damage to monuments or slackness in protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility to identify and communicate locations of monuments
rubrics_metrics.description: Higher commanders must determine the locations of historical monuments through AMG officers, and pass that information down the chain so all commanders can comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance places responsibility on higher commanders and AMG (Allied Military Government) officers to locate monuments 'whether they be immediately ahead of our front lines or in areas occupied by us' and to pass the information to lower echelons through normal channels. This information transmission 'places the responsibility on all commanders of complying with the spirit of this letter.'

rubrics_metrics.name: No use of listed 'Works of Art' buildings for military purposes without explicit permission
rubrics_metrics.description: Buildings listed in the 'Works of Art' sections of the AMG 'Zone Hand-books' will not be used for military purposes except by explicit permission in each individual case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact requirement: 'No building listed in the sections “Works of Art” in the “Zone Hand-books” of Italy... will be used for military purposes without the explicit permission of the Allied Commander‑in‑Chief or of the General Officer Commanding‑in‑Chief, 15th Army Group in each individual case.' This sets a high threshold (explicit central permission) before militarily employing such protected structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to close and secure listed buildings
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders are authorized to close and put out of bounds for troops any buildings listed in the AMG handbooks that they deem necessary and to post notices and guards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'Commanders concerned are authorized... to close and put out of bounds for troops any of the buildings listed in AMG “Zone Hand‑book” that they deem necessary; notices to that effect will be affixed to the buildings, and guards provided to enforce them if necessary.' This allows unit commanders to take local protective measures to prevent inadvertent occupation or damage by their forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision and use of supplementary lists; limited use of secondary‑importance buildings
rubrics_metrics.description: Allied Military Government officers will furnish commanders with lists of historical buildings not in the primary handbook; such secondary‑importance buildings may be used for military purposes when deemed necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance states: 'Allied Military Government officers are prepared to furnish commanders with a list of historical buildings other than those listed in the AMG “Zone‑Hand‑book.” These buildings are of the secondary importance and may be used for military purposes when deemed necessary.' Commanders should request and consult these lists, recognizing that secondary buildings may be employed only when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against looting, wanton damage and sacrilege
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevention of looting, wanton damage and sacrilege of historic buildings is a command responsibility and must be emphasized to all personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'The prevention of looting, wanton damage and sacrilege of buildings is a command responsibility, the seriousness of such an offense will be explained to all Allied personnel.' Commanders must educate and discipline troops to prevent such offenses and enforce protections.
